title: Given \(a > 0\) and \(a + \dfrac{1}{a} = 5\), which statements are correct?

options.note: Multiply both sides by \(a\) to get the quadratic equation.
If \(a=1\), then \(a + \dfrac{1}{a} = 2\), which does not match the condition.
Substituting \(a=5\) does not satisfy the original equation.
The condition does not force \(a\) to be greater than 2.

grading.A: Correct. The original equation becomes a quadratic after multiplying by \(a\).
grading.C: Correct. One of the two quadratic solutions is shown here.
grading.AB: \(B\) is not correct because \(a=1\) does not satisfy the condition.
